recipes.name: Shrimp Rice Bowl
ingredients_raw: 1 orange bell pepper, cut into 1/2-inch dice
1 red bell pepper, cut into 1/2-inch dice

steps.text: Whisk soy sauce, hoisin sauce, honey, orange marmalade, and chili paste together in a small bowl. Stir in shrimp, then cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Bring water and rice to a boil in a saucepan over high heat. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer until rice is tender and all liquid has been absorbed, 20 to 25 minutes.
When the rice is almost finished, heat oil in a large skillet or wok. Add snap peas, bell peppers, and onion and sauté until just beginning to soften, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add marinated shrimp, garlic, ginger, and sesame oil; continue to cook until shrimp is heated through, 2 to 3 more minutes.
Serve shrimp and vegetables over hot rice, sprinkled with sesame seeds.

raw_recipe.headline: Shrimp Rice Bowl
raw_recipe.description: This easy shrimp rice bowl pairs sweet and sour marinated shrimp with lots of fresh vegetables. Served over warm jasmine rice, this dish is full of flavor.

review.reviewBody: The Whole family enjoyed this meal. I made a few changes. I would recommend first stir frying the shrimp and set aside. do not marinate the shrimp because mine got mushy. I pretty much used the same recipe but I didnt have chili paste so i substituted 1/8 teaspoon red pepper flakes. I added some shrooms. I stirfried veggies, then added cooked shrimp and the sauce mixture. For the sauce mixture I reduced garlic to 2 teaspoons because I thought it would be too much. I recommend reducing the ginger to 1 teaspoon because it was too gingering and made my mouth tingle. So I basically used the same recipe except reduced the garlic and ginger and substituted red pepper flakes for the chili paste. Very flavorful and will make it again.

Delicious! Made a few changes based on personal preference / time considerations / ingredients on hand. I used 1/2 teaspoon crushed red pepper flakes instead of the chili paste and apricot marmalade instead of orange. Did not marinate the shrimp. Sauteed the shrimp in the oil first for about 3 mintues until cooked, removed from skillet, and then sauteed the veggies and followed the remaining directions. Made the Jasmine rice in the rice cooker like always. Doubled the shrimp. The veggies I used: 1/2 sweet onion, 1 red pepper, 2 cups sugar snap peas, 1 zuchinni, 1 carrot. Will definitely make again! Had a nice kick, but not too spicy.

Excellent recipe. Stir fried onions, mushrooms in garlic first. . Removed from pan. Used raw shrimp sautéed in butter and garlic. Added sauce before they were done. Added veggies to shrimp mixture along with snow peas. Used oj instead of marmalade and chipotle ketchup spice instead of chili paste. Cooked rice on stove using directions from jasmine package. Was perfect.

I am new to cooking but was able to manage this one! We try to keep the carbs down so I used fried cabbage instead of rice but it came out great. I doubled the batch but my wok was plenty big enough. My wife was surprised at the complexity of flavors in the dish as a lot of stir fry just tastes like soy sauce. If I could do anything different I would have minced the ginger better as the pieces were a little big, but that's on me.
Used sweet Chile sauce rather than paste. Also added 1 tsp chili powder to give it a little more spice. Loved it!

I had a 12 oz bag of raw medium shrimp so I did 1 1/2x the recipe. I marinated the shrimp for almost an hour in the fridge while I chopped all the veggies. I added all the marinade with the shrimp and brought it to a boil to be safe from bacteria and to thicken. I had yellow and green pepper on hand so I used those. Next time I would scale back on the amount of snap peas (just a bit too much) and definitely add in any veggies you have on hand. I used 4 green onions and half a sweet onion. I didn’t have chili paste so I substituted sriracha. It had the perfect amount of spice. I didn’t have orange marmalade so I substituted sweet and sour sauce. I used 5 garlic cloves instead of 6. It just seemed like a lot but 5 was good. The amount of ginger could also be scaled back a bit. However It had very good flavors. I had Zatarrains cilantro lime brown rice which I used. I added 1T fresh cilantro to the rice and sprinkled over the finished dish with some green onion tops, sesame seeds and chopped avocado.

We enjoyed this dish but I found it a bit salty even though I used reduced sodium soy sauce. I’d reduce to 1/4 cup next time. I also thickened the sauce with a teaspoon of cornstarch. Would make again. Thank you!

This was very good! My whole family, including 3 little ones, enjoyed it! The only change I made was using raw shrimp instead of cooked. As written, the recipe did make a lot of extra sauce, but I just used a slotted spoon to add the shrimp to the wok instead of pouring all the sauce in too (and I'm glad I did this). Next time I would reduce the amount of sugar snap peas (just personal preference) and maybe add some different veggies, like mushrooms and broccoli. It's a great versatile recipe, and I will definitely be making this again!

I used raw shrimp and marinated it before cooking, and it had great flavor. I used a variety of vegetables, and after they cooked, I added back the shrimp, Chinese egg noodles and the rest of the sauce. The noodles soaked up most of the sauce, but I would make less next time. It was very good.

I've made this several times. My family loves how fresh it tastes with a great flavor profile. It's very easy and quick to make. I only marinade the shrimp about 30 minutes and have also added chicken.

This was a tasty dish! I added different veggies though...red pepper, white onion, carrots, bean sprouts, mushrooms, broccoli, and snap peas. I also thickened the sauce at the end with a mixture of cornstarch and water. I'll make this again!
Follow the recipe exactly, as we typically do with a first time try. Enjoyed everything. This is a real keeper.
I absolutely love this recipe. It is full a flavor, simple ingredients and easy to follow. I'll defintely make this again and try with chicken or pork next time.
I make it once a week! I will change it up with chicken or fish! My family loves!
New to cooking and made it with minimal changes. Couldn’t find chili paste so subbed in Chile hot sauce. Needed a little more heat but enjoyed it very much and added to favorites
Very good however it was a bit spicy for me. I will definitely make it again however I will use 1/2 the amount of Chili paste.
Delicious!! Reminds me of PF Chang's. I will definitely make this again and again!
Very nice and easy dinner. I let the shrimp marinate overnight and it added the the flavor.

This was delicious!
We use plain brown rice. With the juice from the shrimp & vegetable mix it was outstanding!

Excellent! I made as stated except that i had a 12oz bag of shrimp. I also read that if you marinate the shrimp for an hour it gets soggy so instead I marinated while I was getting everything else ready so around 20-30 minutes. This would be good with other veggies in it too!
